wire.headline: Energy firm reports revenue growth but cuts 850 jobs amid regulatory scrutiny
sentences: The company reported a 7% year-on-year increase in revenue, reaching 4.26bn GBP for the quarter ending 30 September.
Despite the top-line growth, pre-tax profit fell by 12% to 310m GBP.
The firm announced plans to cut 850 jobs, which represents about 6% of its total workforce.
Two gas plants, located in Wales and Kent, are scheduled to close by March 2027.
CEO Marian Holt stated that the pressure on costs has been sharper than the company had anticipated.
The regulator Ofgem has opened an investigation into the company's billing system.
The board decided to hold the dividend at 12.4p a share.
The company's shares fell by 4.2% during morning trading.
